mara.activity: Wake, drink water, open the curtains, and sit at the edge of the bed to sort the presentation, household, and family priorities.
mara.intention: Begin deliberately rather than letting the deadline dictate the whole morning.

mara.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, dress, and carry my laptop and project folder to the office desk.
mara.intention: Get ready without waking the house into a rush.

mara.activity: Make coffee and read the landscape magazine in the living room while the kitchen is available for Julian's breakfast routine.
mara.intention: Have a quiet interval before the day becomes conversational.

mara.activity: Eat a slow breakfast and drink coffee at the kitchen island, keeping notes on the three presentation decisions that still need a defensible answer.
mara.intention: Follow the usual breakfast rhythm while gently organizing the work in my head.

mara.activity: Clear my plate and mug, wash them, and carry the pen, laptop, and mail into the office.
mara.intention: Leave the kitchen orderly before moving into practical planning.

mara.activity: Review household bills and receipts, check the calendar, and make a short priority list at the office desk.
mara.intention: Keep household administration contained so it does not blur into the presentation work.

mara.activity: Prepare a simple lunch, carry it to the dining table, and eat with the visiting relative while keeping conversation warm but bounded.
mara.intention: Offer companionship without surrendering the protected afternoon work period.

mara.activity: Carry the plate and glass back to the kitchen, wash them, and make the work surface clear.
mara.intention: Reset physically before returning to the presentation.

mara.activity: Make a focused final presentation pass at the office desk, checking hierarchy, planting quantities, image captions, and file naming; leave the fabric samples and planting sketches on the desk shelf.
mara.intention: Resolve the details that need to feel coherent rather than merely complete.

mara.activity: Close the laptop, carry it and the project folder aside, then take a brisk walk around the neighborhood before answering messages.
mara.intention: Release the controlled pressure before making any decisions or responding to anyone.

mara.activity: Return home, put my keys in the open entryway while removing my shoes, carry the field notebook to the living room sideboard, and sit briefly with the relative.
mara.intention: Re-enter the shared house calmly and maintain an affectionate but manageable rhythm.

mara.activity: Gather the ingredients and clear the kitchen island for the planned large meal.
mara.intention: Shift from work to cooking without bringing the presentation's tension into the kitchen.

mara.activity: Prepare a large meal for leftovers, portion it into food storage bags, and leave the main cooking area ready for Julian's evening kitchen routine.
mara.intention: Make the practical, generous meal that will simplify the coming days.

mara.activity: Carry a serving portion and a water glass to the dining table, eat a modest dinner with the household, and keep conversation easy.
mara.intention: Be present without turning dinner into another performance of hosting.

mara.activity: Carry my plate and glass back to the kitchen, wash them, and put the remaining meal away neatly.
mara.intention: Finish my part of the evening's kitchen work while Julian takes over his cooking routine.

mara.activity: Retreat to the piano hall with the lights low and play a few slow scales, leaving the music area quiet afterward.
mara.intention: Reduce stimulation and let the final presentation judgments settle.

mara.activity: Take a quiet shower, change into comfortable clothes, and check in briefly with the relative before returning to the bedroom.
mara.intention: Keep the evening warm while protecting a clear boundary around rest.

mara.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, and prepare the bed; leave the laptop and project folder out of the bedroom.
mara.intention: End work decisively rather than carrying it into sleep.

mara.activity: Read quietly in bed, then place my reading glasses on the top of my nightstand and sleep.
mara.intention: Let the day close without checking work messages.

julian.activity: Wake quietly, wash, brush my teeth, and get dressed in lounge clothes. I carry my phone charger from the nightstand only if needed, then leave the bedroom without waking anyone.
julian.intention: Start slowly and give Mara and the visiting relative a quiet house.

julian.activity: Make coffee and carry a mug to the kitchen island. I grind the beans, add milk, and sit with the mug while I look over the kitchen and decide on a simple breakfast.
julian.intention: Ease into the morning without creating conversation or decisions.

julian.activity: Make pancakes and eggs while Mara reads nearby. I carry the mixing bowl and ingredients to the island, whisk the batter, warm butter in the skillet, and cook the eggs gently so the edges turn lacy while the centers stay soft. I carry plates, forks, and mugs to the island, serve breakfast, then carry the used dishes to the sink and rinse them.
julian.intention: Keep to our familiar Sunday breakfast while making the kitchen feel warm and easy.

julian.activity: Wipe the island and cooktop, put the skillet and mixing bowl beside the sink, and make a small packed lunch for the walk. I fill a water bottle and leave the kitchen orderly without beginning a larger project.
julian.intention: Finish one task cleanly before leaving the house.

julian.activity: Get ready to go out. I put on jeans, a hoodie, jacket, and walking shoes, take my wallet and phone, and pick up the packed food and water bottle. I leave my house keys on the piano's middle shelf until the last moment, then carry them with me.
julian.intention: Take a restorative break away from family conversation and restaurant concerns.

julian.activity: Take a long walk with lunch away from the restaurant and the house. I eat the packed fruit and a simple lunch, drink water, and let the pace stay unhurried rather than turning it into exercise or errands.
julian.intention: Recover physically and have a stretch of uncomplicated time.

julian.activity: Return home, put my keys on the piano's middle shelf, take off my jacket and hoodie, and carry the water bottle to the kitchen. I wash my hands and sit somewhere quiet for a few minutes instead of joining a long conversation immediately.
julian.intention: Re-enter the house gently and preserve some solitude.

julian.activity: Have a quiet rest with a paperback book. I carry the book to the living room sectional, leave my phone face down on the coffee table, and read until my mind stops running through restaurant lists.
julian.intention: Recover from the week without television or demanding interaction.

julian.activity: Make tea and carry a mug to the piano. I put the tea on the side table, stretch my hands, and bring my music notebook and metronome from their usual places.
julian.intention: Shift into a calm, focused activity.

julian.activity: Practice piano and play through new melodies. I work quietly at first, marking a few changes in the music notebook, then play the promising passage louder for a few minutes. I leave the notebook and metronome on the piano shelf when finished.
julian.intention: Have a private creative hour and let the house settle around me.

julian.activity: Take a shower or change into comfortable cooking clothes, then give Mara the kitchen while she prepares the large meal. I stay available to carry something or wash a utensil if asked, but otherwise spend the time in the living room with the relative for a bounded, friendly visit.
julian.intention: Be generous without crowding Mara's focused cooking or exhausting myself before dinner.

julian.activity: Take over the kitchen for dinner and the week's portions. I carry the stockpot and saucepan to the range, warm the meal, adjust it with salt and herbs, and portion leftovers into containers. I set out bowls, spoons, napkins, and a serving platter, then carry the used cookware to the sink and wipe the counters.
julian.intention: Turn the evening meal into a reassuring, organized routine and make the next few days easier.

julian.activity: Carry a bowl and water glass to the table, eat a modest serving, and keep conversation light. I rinse the bowl and spoon afterward, leave them beside the sink, and carry a mug of tea to the living room if the relative is still there.
julian.intention: Eat enough to recover without turning the end of the day into another event.

julian.activity: Put the kitchen into a safe stopping point, carry my wallet and earplugs to the living room coffee table, and check that my phone is charging. I avoid television and keep the lights low.
julian.intention: Begin the quiet, familiar wind-down I need after the weekend.

julian.activity: Brush my teeth, wash my face, and change into sleep clothes. I carry the towel back toward the bathroom, leave it there to dry, and bring my phone to the main bedroom nightstand.
julian.intention: Finish the night with as few decisions as possible.

julian.activity: Get into the main bedroom bed beside Mara, put the phone on its charger, and settle under the covers without turning on the television. I use the sleep mask if the room is still bright and go to sleep.
julian.intention: Recover fully before the demanding week begins.
